scenario.title: Geodesign Barriers Ltd v The Environment Agency
scenario.description: The Plaintiff, Geodesign Barriers Ltd, challenged the evaluation process of a tender for temporary flood barrier systems conducted by the Defendant, The Environment Agency. The Plaintiff alleged that the successful bid did not comply with mandatory performance specifications and requested specific disclosure of documents, including Tender Evaluation Reports, guidance emails, and bids of other tenderers. The court granted in part and refused in part the Plaintiff's applications, ordering disclosure of category C and E documents, but rejecting the request for identities of other unsuccessful tenderers. The confidentiality ring was ordered to include one expert alongside lawyers.

interests: Compliance & Legality: Ensure the evaluation process was lawful and within powers under the Procurement Act 2023.
Protection of Public Funds: Avoid delays that increase costs, given the £0 contract value.
Continuity of Service / Delivery: Maintain critical flood protection services for communities at risk.
Reputation & Public Accountability: Uphold public confidence in our procurement process and protect our reputation as a competent buyer.
ca_pre_negotiation.batna: Defend the decision in the TCC — costly (£50k+) and slow (6-12 months), with a real risk of automatic suspension.
ca_pre_negotiation.opening_position: We will provide additional disclosure as ordered by the court, but stand firm on maintaining confidentiality for other unsuccessful tenderers.

interests: Commercial Loss & Recovery: We invested £150,000 in this bid, including staff time and external consultants, which we won't recover if the contract is awarded to another bidder.
Fairness & Transparency: The evaluation process was opaque and inconsistent, with no clear explanation for why our bid was rejected despite meeting all mandatory performance specifications.
goals: Force a re-evaluation of submitted bids
bidder_pre_negotiation.batna: Pursue a damages claim in the TCC — costly (£50k-£100k in legal fees) for a business our size, slow, and the outcome is uncertain.
bidder_pre_negotiation.opening_position: We request full disclosure of all evaluation documents, including Tender Evaluation Reports, guidance emails, and bids of other tenderers, to ensure transparency and fairness in this procurement process.

messages.message: Geodesign Barriers Ltd's opening position highlights concerns regarding the evaluation process and disclosure of documents. I'd like to clarify whether their challenge is focused on a specific aspect of the evaluation, such as scoring or compliance with performance specifications. Can you provide more context on what they believe was inaccurately evaluated or improperly disclosed? Additionally, I'd like to offer an initial concession by providing the category C and E documents that were ordered to be disclosed, as well as any guidance emails related to those categories.
messages.concession_made: Providing category C and E documents and relevant guidance emails

messages.message: Thank you for your response and concession to disclose category C and E documents. I'd like to clarify whether this disclosure includes all relevant documentation, including any scoring sheets or evaluation matrices used by the evaluation panel. Furthermore, can you confirm that the guidance emails related to categories C and E will be provided in their entirety, without redactions or omissions? We appreciate your willingness to provide transparency, but we believe it is essential to understand the full context of the evaluation process.

We understand your request for clarification on the disclosure of scoring sheets and evaluation matrices used by the evaluation panel. While we cannot disclose these documents in their entirety, as they contain commercially sensitive information about other bidders, we are willing to provide a summary of the evaluation process and the criteria used to assess each bid. This will include an explanation of how the scores were allocated and the reasoning behind the successful bidder's selection. We believe this will provide sufficient transparency into our evaluation process without compromising confidentiality.
messages.concession_made: Disclosure of a summary of the evaluation process and criteria used to assess each bid

messages.message: We appreciate your willingness to provide transparency into your evaluation process. However, we believe that a summary of the evaluation process and criteria used is insufficient without access to the scoring sheets and evaluation matrices. These documents are essential for us to understand how our bid was assessed and why we were not selected as the successful bidder. We request that you reconsider disclosing these documents in their entirety, or at least provide a detailed explanation of how they can be made available to us while maintaining confidentiality about other bidders.

We understand that the disclosure of scoring sheets and evaluation matrices is crucial for your understanding of our evaluation process. In light of this, we are willing to provide a detailed explanation of how these documents can be made available to you while maintaining confidentiality about other bidders. We propose creating a redacted version of the scoring sheets and evaluation matrices, removing any commercially sensitive information related to other bidders, and providing this to you in addition to our previous concessions.
messages.proposal: Redacted Scoring Sheets and Evaluation Matrices

messages.message: We appreciate your proposal to create a redacted version of the scoring sheets and evaluation matrices, removing any commercially sensitive information related to other bidders. However, we believe that this compromise still falls short of providing us with a complete understanding of the evaluation process. We are willing to accept this concession as part of a final agreement, but only if it is accompanied by a formal apology for the perceived unfairness in the evaluation process and a commitment from The Environment Agency to review its evaluation procedures to prevent similar issues in future tenders.
messages.concession_made: acceptance of redacted scoring sheets and evaluation matrices

compliance_checks.reasoning: This scenario is qualitative, as it involves the evaluation of tender documents and compliance with performance specifications. There are no explicit formulas or sub-scores mentioned in the scenario. The Contracting Authority's concession to disclose category C and E documents suggests a willingness to provide transparency, which aligns with the principles of fairness and transparency outlined in the Procurement Act 2023 s12. However, the Aggrieved Bidder's request for scoring sheets or evaluation matrices used by the evaluation panel raises concerns about the completeness of the disclosure.

applicable_provisions: The Public Contracts Regulations 2015, Regulation 86(1) and (3); The Freedom of Information Act 2000
compliance_checks.reasoning: This scenario is qualitative in nature. There are no explicit formulas or sub-scores mentioned. The parties' positions focus on the disclosure of documents, specifically scoring sheets and evaluation matrices. I will assess compliance qualitatively instead. The Contracting Authority has offered to provide a summary of the evaluation process and criteria used, which includes an explanation of how scores were allocated and the reasoning behind the successful bidder's selection. This appears to be in line with the principles of transparency and fairness. However, the Aggrieved Bidder is seeking access to the scoring sheets and evaluation matrices, which may contain commercially sensitive information about other bidders. The Contracting Authority has a legitimate concern for maintaining confidentiality. I will not conclude that there is a manifest error based on this information.

ca_win_statement.outcome_relative_to_batna: The final outcome is somewhat favorable compared to our BATNA, which would have involved a lengthy and costly court battle. While we did not concede on all points, we were able to limit the disclosure of sensitive information and maintain some confidentiality.
ca_win_statement.win_statement: We successfully defended our evaluation process and maintained transparency while protecting commercially sensitive information from other bidders. We also demonstrated flexibility in finding a compromise that met the aggrieved bidder's concerns without compromising our position.
what_was_achieved: Disclosed category C and E documents, as well as guidance emails related to those categories
Provided a summary of the evaluation process and criteria used to assess each bid
Created a redacted version of scoring sheets and evaluation matrices
what_was_conceded: Disclosure of some commercially sensitive information about other bidders
A formal apology for perceived unfairness in the evaluation process (not explicitly agreed upon, but implied as part of the final agreement)
Commitment to review evaluation procedures to prevent similar issues in future tenders

bidder_win_statement.outcome_relative_to_batna: The final outcome is slightly better than our BATNA, as we were able to secure some concessions from the contracting authority, including disclosure of category C and E documents, guidance emails, and a redacted version of scoring sheets and evaluation matrices. However, we did not achieve our desired goal of full disclosure of these documents, and the decision stands without any formal apology or commitment to review their evaluation procedures.
bidder_win_statement.win_statement: We were able to negotiate some concessions from the contracting authority, including additional transparency into their evaluation process, but ultimately fell short of securing a more favorable outcome for our client.
what_was_achieved: Disclosure of category C and E documents
Guidance emails related to categories C and E
Redacted version of scoring sheets and evaluation matrices
what_was_conceded: Full disclosure of scoring sheets and evaluation matrices
Formal apology for perceived unfairness in the evaluation process
Commitment from The Environment Agency to review its evaluation procedures

key_sticking_points: Disclosure of scoring sheets and evaluation matrices used by the evaluation panel
Commercially sensitive information about other bidders
Transparency and fairness in the evaluation process
summary.concessions_summary: The Contracting Authority made several concessions, including: (1) providing category C and E documents, (2) disclosing a summary of the evaluation process and criteria used to assess each bid, and (3) offering to create a redacted version of the scoring sheets and evaluation matrices.
summary.court_reasoning_summary: The Court assessed each round qualitatively, considering the principles of transparency and fairness outlined in the Procurement Act 2023 s12. The Court recognized the Contracting Authority's willingness to provide transparency but also acknowledged its legitimate concerns about maintaining confidentiality. Ultimately, the Court concluded that there was no manifest error and recommended no remedy.
summary.likely_next_steps: Given the Court's decision, it is likely that the Aggrieved Bidder will not pursue further action. The Contracting Authority may review its evaluation procedures to prevent similar issues in future tenders, as requested by the Aggrieved Bidder, but this is not a formal requirement.
summary.plain_english_summary: The negotiation centered around the disclosure of documents related to the evaluation process. While the Contracting Authority made concessions to provide transparency, the Aggrieved Bidder continued to push for access to scoring sheets and evaluation matrices. The Court ultimately decided that there was no manifest error and that the decision stands.
